Introduction

This guidance will help you to:

understand the benefits of using smartphones and devices in adult social care

decide whether to provide staff with smartphones or allow the use of personal devices

understand the risks involved in using smartphones and how to keep them safe

There are 2 options for introducing smartphones and other mobile devices at your organisation:

provide company phones

use software that is designed so staff can use their personal devices

The main factors in this decision include cost and safety, as well as what you want to use the devices for.

Comparing company and personal devices

Providing company devices

Advantages include:

easier to make sure they’re managed securely

better oversight

Disadvantages include:

higher cost

may need technical expertise to manage

staff less familiar with using device

Providing personal devices

Advantages include:

more cost effective

staff already comfortable with using device

Disadvantages include:

less secure

need to enforce a ‘bring your own device’ policy

less oversight

Decide what you’ll need them for

To decide which route to take, consider how you plan on using smartphones and other devices in your organisation. There are 3 levels of tasks you might use them for, which are:

communication

paperless systems

core operations

Level 1 - communication

This is using smartphones as a communication device only, so staff can co-ordinate care more efficiently and collaborate with others.

Uses

This allows you to centralise messaging, reducing the need for official updates and informal conversations across your organisation.

What you need

A messaging app with licences for staff.

How to be safe

Train staff in code of conduct and UK General Data Protection Regulations (UK GDPR) compliance. For example:

not sharing identifiable information about clients or photos of them

using strong passwords

spotting abuse or malice

reporting bad conduct

reporting data breaches if their phone is lost or stolen

What to do

If you use devices for less official communications such as travel conditions and changes to timings, then you could ask staff to bring their own. Set up an account on a simple messaging platform and train staff to use it on their own device.

You could use:

Microsoft Teams - a messaging platform included with Office 365, which lets you set up groups and include third party apps for tasks such as editing documents remotely

enterprise social networks such as Slack or Yammer - these are like internal social media, but you can control the groups staff are in to some extent (most social networks have a free version or can cost around £10 to £20 for full functionality)

Facebook or WhatsApp - it’s important to make sure these are used safely

Level 2 - paperless systems

This means using mobile devices to access digital admin systems, such as annual leave systems, policy libraries and rota information (sometimes called an ‘intranet’). It replaces the need to send out rotas and forms to the whole company.

Uses

Paperless systems allow staff to access information and systems that are relevant to them from their device. For example, so they can book leave or see their schedule.

What you need

Software that allows each person to access an account from a mobile device.

How to be safe

Only allow staff to access information that’s relevant to them on the system, and provide training on code of conduct and UK GDPR compliance.

What to do

You could allow staff to bring their own devices, as long as you provide comprehensive training and clear processes. Make sure staff understand which information is stored where while accessing the intranet and how to keep it safe.

Alternatively, provide a company phone with the system already installed to make sure it’s easy to use it correctly and safely. You could select a senior team to receive these phones and manage most of the intranet, providing only basic access to other staff.

You could use software such as:

Microsoft SharePoint - a cloud storage system included with Office 365, it allows documents, videos and photos to be stored and organised in the way you choose, and you can give different access permissions to different staff

Interact - a similar system designed specifically for healthcare (though not specifically social care)

Level 3 - core operations

This is using mobile devices to allow support workers, co-ordinators and managers to carry out everyday tasks remotely and instantly.

Uses

This allows you to carry out tasks remotely such as:

logging in and out of visits

sending updates about a person’s conditions

designing and reviewing care plans

What you need

Care software that works safely with smartphones and other devices.

How to be safe

You will need:

complete governance covering smartphones, including how to keep all software up to date

contingency plans, plans for phones breaking or being lost or stolen, misused or hacked

regular staff training on UK GDPR compliance, digital skills and digital safety

contracts that outline staff responsibilities related to the devices

to check the phone for appropriateness and safety, if allowing personal devices

What to do

In most cases, it’s better to provide company devices.

To bring the cost down, consider which staff need full access to all systems and who needs a device at what point. Some providers keep devices fixed in safe locations and allow care workers to sign into these with their own accounts during their shift, but not take them away from these locations.

Consider how devices can connect to the internet, especially if care workers are moving around or in rural areas.

Care software usually includes safety measures and updates, but you may still need mobile device management software or a clear policy about use.

If you allow staff to use their own devices you should have appropriate safeguards in place. This is sometimes called ‘bring your own device’ and includes:

having a clear policy

completing a data protection impact assessment

using secure and approved apps

ensuring work data is kept separate from personal information

You should also make sure staff understand how to follow your organisation’s policies and use devices securely. Fully unmanaged use of personal devices presents the highest level of risk and should be avoided.
